key_impacts: By 11 May 2020, nearly 4.2 million cases and 284,000 deaths were reported globally.
COVID-19 epidemics can rapidly exceed healthcare capacity, including in high-income countries such as the US and Italy.
Modeling estimates a 32.0% higher death probability in the poorest versus wealthiest quintile due to handwashing, occupation, and healthcare access differences.
An estimated 2.01 billion people lack access to handwashing facilities, limiting basic infection prevention, especially in LICs/LMICs.
Timing in low-resource settings may interrupt planting and harvesting seasons for staple crops, heightening food security vulnerabilities.
